## analyze_token

- Title: Analyze token
- Profile: `core` (default)
- Annotations: `openWorldHint: true`, `readOnlyHint: true`

(Recommended for token research) Analyze a Sui coin type or symbol: metadata, current price, 24h change, supply, top holders and current pool-liquidity custody. Verified symbols resolve from the curated list; other mainnet symbols use DexScreener and GeckoTerminal searches confirmed on chain, several exact matches return ambiguous_symbol, and a provider cap or failed confirmation is reported, not read as an absent coin. Pool search covers SUI and native-USDC pairs with per-venue failure reporting. Liquidity custody scans the three pools with the largest SUI or USDC reserve; a stopped holder scan never establishes ownership concentration. Set include_liquidity false to skip pool reads.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query` | string | yes | Symbol ('deep') or full coin type ('0x2::sui::SUI'). A symbol matches exactly, in any case; use search_token for partial names. |
| `include_holders` | boolean | no | Include top 5 holders (default: true). Set false for faster response. |
| `holder_max_scan` | integer (1 to 50000) | no | Coin objects and address balances scanned per holder walk (default 2000, max 50000). |
| `holder_time_budget_ms` | integer (1000 to 600000) | no | Holder scan wall-clock budget in milliseconds (default 35000, max 600000). |
| `include_liquidity` | boolean | no | Inspect current liquidity and its LP or position holders in up to three discovered pools (default: true). Set false for metadata-only calls. |
| `liquidity_pool_offset` | integer (at least 0) | no | Start at this discovered pool after ranking by its current SUI or USDC reserve (default 0). |
| `liquidity_holder_pool` | string | no | For a holder continuation, restrict the page to this discovered pool ID. |
| `liquidity_offset` | integer (at least 0) | no | Start at this holder index within liquidity_holder_pool (default 0). |
| `liquidity_flagged_done` | boolean | no | Holder-page continuation marker; keep the value from omitted.next_call to avoid repeating flagged holders. |
| `liquidity_max_scan` | integer (1 to 100000) | no | Max LP coins or position objects scanned per pool (default 1000, max 100000); follow liquidity_custody.pools[].scan.next_call after a bound. |
| `liquidity_time_budget_ms` | integer (1000 to 600000) | no | Wall-clock budget for pool position scans in milliseconds (default 35000, max 600000). |
| `liquidity_venue` | string | no | Search one venue; use pool_discovery.venues[].next_call to continue a bounded venue search. |
| `liquidity_venue_cursor` | string | no | Opaque per-venue cursor; resumes discovery over both SUI and USDC pairs. |
| `network` | `mainnet` \| `testnet` \| `devnet` | no | Network: 'mainnet' (default) \| 'testnet' \| 'devnet' |

## get_transaction_history

- Title: Get transaction history
- Profile: `core` (default)
- Annotations: `openWorldHint: true`, `readOnlyHint: true`

(Recommended for wallet activity) Read a wallet's decoded protocols, actions and coin flows; prefer this to query_transactions for exploring activity. from/to bound the chain query: ISO times are inclusive, checkpoint numbers exclusive. Rows use complete balance changes and commands. Newest first by default; oldest starts at the first transaction in the window. Pass next_cursor as cursor with the same from, to and order. address_poisoning always checks the shown page only, so empty pairs clear nothing older. subject_flow is the queried wallet's signed change per coin; token_flow is the sender's, omitted when they are the same address. Counterparties include at most 25 value recipients; counterparty_count reports larger sets. Summary keeps ~35k characters, preserving failed and lookalike-involved rows; omitted reports the rest and detail:'full' lists the whole page. signed_as_alias separately lists transactions signed as another wallet's address_alias delegate, which the main page cannot show. The delegate scan is cached for up to five minutes; alias_scan_as_of dates it and signed_as_alias_unavailable marks incomplete scans, even beside returned matches.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | yes | Sui wallet address (0x...) |
| `from` | string | no | Inclusive window start as ISO 8601 time or exclusive after-checkpoint number. |
| `to` | string | no | Inclusive window end as ISO 8601 time, 'now', or exclusive before-checkpoint number. |
| `limit` | number (1 to 50), default `10` | no | Number of transactions to return (default 10, max 50) |
| `order` | `newest` \| `oldest` | no | 'newest' (default) pages backward from recent activity; 'oldest' pages forward from the first transaction. |
| `cursor` | string | no | `next_cursor` from the previous page. Continues in the same direction; pass the same `order`, `from` and `to`. |
| `detail` | `summary` \| `full` | no | 'summary' (default) keeps ~35k chars in page order, always retaining failed and lookalike-involved rows; omitted reports the rest. 'full' lists every row of the page. |
| `network` | `mainnet` \| `testnet` \| `devnet` | no | Network: 'mainnet' (default) \| 'testnet' \| 'devnet' |

## get_wallet_overview

- Title: Get wallet overview
- Profile: `core` (default)
- Annotations: `openWorldHint: true`, `readOnlyHint: true`

(Recommended first tool for wallets) Overview of a Sui wallet: every coin balance, SuiNS name, staked SUI and kiosk counts, 50 newest transactions with an older-history continuation, and a time-bounded scan of package versions it published or upgraded in the first 20 sent transactions (`package_activity.scan.next_call` continues; `package_activity_next_call` retries if unavailable). include_prices adds USD values, coins ranked by value, and DeFi positions (staked SUI with rewards, liquid staking, liquidity, lending, and balances inside owned objects), each totalled apart. `coverage` says which owned objects the total covers and lists unrecognised types with counts; `leads` names lending positions near their borrow limit and shared vaults the wallet operates, with what they hold. include_nfts adds NFT estimates, kept out of the total.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | yes | Wallet address (0x...) |
| `include_prices` | boolean | no | Add USD values, DeFi positions, coverage and leads (default: false). |
| `include_nfts` | boolean | no | With include_prices, also estimate held NFTs (default: false). Takes many requests on a wallet with many objects; list_nft_collections does this alone. |
| `balance_cursor` | string | no | Opaque balance cursor from holdings_next_call. Returns the next bounded block of coin types; totals cover only this block. |
| `owned_max_scan` | integer (1 to 50000) | no | Raise owned-object and position scan bounds for include_prices (defaults vary by reader); unread still reports any incomplete read. |
| `nft_max_collections` | integer (1 to 5000) | no | NFT collection types valued with include_nfts (default 100); raise through nft_scan_next_call. |
| `nft_market_depth` | integer (1 to 20) | no | Multiplier for bounded NFT market listing/sale reads (default 1); raise through nft_market_next_call. |
| `operated_recent_limit` | integer (1 to 50) | no | Sent transactions per operated-shared-object scan page (default 20). |
| `operated_candidate_limit` | integer (1 to 500) | no | Shared objects checked per operated scan page (default 20). |
| `operated_cursor` | string | no | Older sent-transaction cursor from operated_scan.next_call. |
| `detail` | `summary` \| `full` | no | 'summary' (default): holdings and unrecognised object types that fit about 12k characters each, the rest in `omitted`. 'full': every row. |
| `network` | `mainnet` \| `testnet` \| `devnet` | no | Network: 'mainnet' (default) \| 'testnet' \| 'devnet' |

## get_wallet_packages

- Title: Get wallet packages
- Profile: `core` (default)
- Annotations: `openWorldHint: true`, `readOnlyHint: true`

List package versions created by publish or upgrade transactions sent from this wallet address. Scans 20 sent transactions per call, oldest first; `scan.complete` is true only when all pages and transactions were read. `scan.next_call` continues with an opaque cursor that carries prior unread counts. `scan.incomplete_transactions` names unread digests on this page and `scan.prior_incomplete_transactions` counts them on earlier pages. Each package carries its creating transaction, lineage root and version; an alias may have signed for the sender, and the sender is not necessarily the current UpgradeCap holder.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | yes | Wallet address (0x...) |
| `cursor` | string | no | Opaque cursor from scan.next_call, to scan the next 20 sent transactions. |
| `network` | `mainnet` \| `testnet` \| `devnet` | no | Network: 'mainnet' (default) \| 'testnet' \| 'devnet' |

## identify_address

- Title: Identify address
- Profile: `core` (default)
- Annotations: `openWorldHint: true`, `readOnlyHint: true`

(Recommended first step) Classify a Sui address as wallet, package, validator or object before choosing other tools. For wallets, package_activity scans the first 20 sent transactions for publishes/upgrades and provides next_call to continue; the result also includes balance and name context. Package results include modules and bridge labels on defined objects; bridge_carrier identifies bytecode calls into curated bridge exits. Validator results include stake information. A wallet's first_seen is the oldest transaction GraphQL returns where it sent or was affected, with received coins read across all balance-change pages. first_inflow means it gained coins without sending, including genesis with sender:null; genesis names no funding wallet. Incomplete balance changes with no observed gain leave first_inflow null. first_seen_unavailable marks a failed first read. Use find_funding_sources when the first transaction was only a token airdrop.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `address` | string | yes | Sui address or object ID (0x...) |
| `network` | `mainnet` \| `testnet` \| `devnet` | no | Network: 'mainnet' (default) \| 'testnet' \| 'devnet' |
